text.p: Bonds recovered from the lows to which they plunged on remarks by a Bundesbank Council member that Italy would not make the start of monetary union.
The benchmark 10-year cash bond ended nearly 50 basis points up on the day and traders see the potential for further gains, although the market will remain volatile.
Bundesbank Council member Klaus-Dieter Kuehbacher said that Italy should not take part in the launch of monetary union as it did not fulfill some of the entry criteria.
"After these remarks, Italian debt slipped and brought Spain and Portugal down with it," said one trader.

Traders said that the Portuguese market did not fall as far as Spain because of the lack of local liquidity. Some support also came from the notion that Portugal is in better shape than the other two candidates to qualify for the single currency, traders added.
